source.title: Clogher Rural District, "Notice of Result of Elections: Election of Rural District Councillors for the above-named Rural District in the Year 1899", dated 7 April 1899, H. Irvine, returning officer (PRONI LA/24/3/AD/1; the owner's photographs of 10 November 2026, frames 403 and 405); compared with the Tyrone Constitution, 14 April 1899, p. 7 ("Elections: Result of the Polling in Tyrone")
source.publisher: Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (Clogher Rural District Council records)
source.check: read from the owner's photographs of the printed notice in two blind transcriptions by separate readers, which agreed on every name, figure and mark; a script checked that each division elects as many as its seats and that the elected are the top of the poll; abodes are not published

note: First election of the rural district council, held with the election of the board of guardians: each district electoral division returned its councillors, who were also its guardians. Polled in April 1899 and declared on Friday 7 April 1899 at the union boardroom (Tyrone Constitution, 14 April 1899, p. 7, "Elections: Result of the Polling in Tyrone"); the poll date, Thursday 6 April, is the day before the declaration and is still to be confirmed from a sentence in a newspaper. Cullamore returned 2 councillors, unopposed. The notice prints three names for Cullamore, but Patrick Hackett's line is struck through by hand on the notice, and the Tyrone Constitution (14 April 1899, p. 7) lists only John Connolly, junior, and John M'Kenna for the division; it is filed with those two.
